title: SLO Shadowing Service and Anomaly Rescoring Playbook
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Objective: Build a temporary 'SLO Shadowing' service that mirrors production telemetry (traces/metrics/logs) into an isolated pipeline to evaluate new anomaly-rescoring models and burn-rate heuristics without impacting live alerts or oncall. The service couples lightweight trace hooks at the edge, a metrics reshaper stage, and a parallel alert-scoring layer so PM/Oncall can validate regressions and tune paging policies before rollout.

Background: Our SLO alerts have become brittle for mixed-latency workloads where KV-cache warmups and batched tails produce intermittent spikes. We need a low-risk path to test new anomaly detectors and weighting strategies against real traffic, capture false-positive/negative metrics, and iterate on paging policy changes. Shadowing lets us run experiments and gather labeled outcomes (pager/no-pager, severity, root-cause tags) without touching production paging.

Goals: 
- Implement a lightweight shadow pipeline that receives copies of span and metric events with minimal added latency on the main path.
- Reshape metrics for consistent SLI calculation (normalize histograms, synthesize request-context tags).
- Run anomaly-rescoring models on the shadow stream and record scoring outputs alongside ground-truth incidents.
- Expose dashboards for evaluation: per-model precision/recall, false-positive heatmap, and cost-latency trade-offs.
- Produce a runnable playbook for rolling candidate scoring into canary alerts with rollback triggers.

Non-goals: Do not change production alerting routes or oncall policies during shadow experiments. This is analysis-only until explicit rollout decision.

Success criteria: 
- Shadow pipeline ingests >=95% of sampled production traces for target services for a 48-hour trial.
- Anomaly rescoring model demonstrates >=20% reduction in false-positive pagers on benchmark prompt set while keeping mean time to detect within 1.2x baseline.
- Dashboards and exportable CSVs allow SRE and PM to make a yes/no rollout decision within two business days.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Added latency on main path: use non-blocking, UDP-like forwarding to shadow queue; enforce a 200ms budget for the sidecar forward call.
- Data privacy: strip PII at the trace-hook layer and respect redaction rules; run shadow pipeline in VPC-isolated namespace.
- Observability noise: implement deterministic sampling controls and a replay mode to ensure consistent comparisons.

Notes: This ticket coordinates with the tracing ingestion team (ENG-74211) for hook API stability and the SLO eval framework (ENG-21813) for consistent SLI calculations.
implementation_steps: Design trace-hook contract: minimal metadata, redaction rules, sampling key (owner/service/route). Draft API (proto + http fallback).
Add non-blocking edge forwarder in runtime that duplicates spans to a shadow topic (Kafka/SQS) with schema v1-shadow. Apply redaction and tag synthesis.
Build metrics reshaper microservice: consumes shadow spans, extracts SLIs, normalizes histograms and produces canonical metric streams for the rescoring models.
Integrate anomaly-rescoring models: containerize two candidate models (statistical baseline + gradient model) and run them side-by-side on shadow stream. Persist scores and thresholds.
Create evaluation dashboards: precision/recall, per-service false-positive heatmap, latency distribution pre/post-scoring, and incident matching overlays.
Run 48-hour shadow trial on two services (runtime-api, embeddings-ingest). Collect labeled incidents and compare against current burn-rate alerts.
Hold cross-functional review with SRE/PM/Design to finalize rollout criteria and canary plan. Prepare rollback thresholds and automation.
acceptance_criteria: Shadow forwarder present in runtime-proxy with config toggle and no more than 200ms tail impact on 99th percentile calls.
Shadow topic retention, schema, and consumer group documented; no PII persisted in shadow pipeline.
Evaluation dashboards populated and accessible to SRE+PM; CSV export for offline analysis.
Comparison report showing model metrics and recommended threshold for canary traffic.
